This dossier starts the state at the Tang fall in 907 so that the 908 loss to Chu lies inside its life.

keyframe_review.note: Valid for 911-946, and with the 947 verdict to 950. Cliopatria's 322,737 km2 includes northern Vietnam (bbox down to 17.77 N, countries China and Vietnam) and ends at 'Ngo dynasty' in 947. The Bach Dang page calls Jinghai 'a Viet principality' that Southern Han attacked in October 930, lost again in 931 ('Duong Dinh Nghe ... drove the Southern Han back to the circuit's borders') and failed to retake in 938, so Vietnam is not Southern Han land except Oct 930-931 (occupation events). By the project's cell count Vietnam is 204 of the shape's 1,185 cells (17 percent), and the shape without it (981 cells) matches the Cliopatria 947 shape (979 cells), so the 947 change is exactly the Vietnam cut. No infobox area exists on the Southern Han page, so no ratio. Disagrees with the ngo-dynasty dossier, which has Ngo founded in 939 out of southern-han land (see notes).

region.text: the Guangzhou command, Guangdong, Guangxi and Hainan

ledger.note: 907: the Tang falls and Liu Yin keeps the south coast. 'Named regional governor and military officer by the Tang court in 905', he 'did not declare a new kingdom after the Tang fell'; the kingdom came in 917. The page gives no area; the extent is the Cliopatria shape without Vietnam.

region.text: the northeastern Guangxi prefectures taken from Liu Yin in 908 (Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, Fu)

ledger.note: 908: Ma Yin takes six prefectures from Liu Yin. 'Ma also sent Lü Shizhou to attack the territory of Liu Yin' and captured 'six prefectures from Liu Yin: Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, and Fu'. The page does not locate them; the Ma Chu page's 'northeastern Guangxi' reads them as the Wuzhou country (as in the southern-chu dossier).

917: Liu Yan proclaims a kingdom, Yue. He 'declared the founding of a new kingdom, which he initially called Yue (越)' after Liu Yin's death (the page dates the death to 917, the Ma Yin page has Liu Yan already ruling in 913).
918: the realm is renamed Han. 'He changed the name to Han (漢) in 918', claiming descent from the Han dynasty through his Liu surname.

region.text: the Jinghai circuit, a Viet principality in northern Vietnam

ledger.note: 930: Southern Han attacks Jinghai. The Southern Han forces 'launched an attack on the Jinghai circuit, which at the time was a Viet principality' in October 930 and the Khuc leader was taken prisoner. The page does not say the land was annexed; it says Duong Dinh Nghe drove the Han back in 931, so a one-year occupation is drawn.

931: Duong Dinh Nghe drives the Han out. 'In 931, the local general Duong Dinh Nghe raised a 3,000-men army of retainers' and pushed the Southern Han back to the circuit's borders; the page gives no month.

971: the Song take Guangzhou and end the Southern Han. 'Northern Song forces captured the Southern Han capital of Guangzhou' (campaign 970-971); Liu Chang surrendered; the page gives no month.

wars.outcome: Ma Yin took six prefectures (Zhao, He, Wu, Meng, Gong, Fu) in 908; Liu Yin took Rong and Gao in 911 after Ma's man Yao Yanzhang withdrew; Emperor Taizu brokered peace in 911 and Liu Yan married into the Ma family in 913-915.

wars.name: Southern Han invasions of Jinghai
wars.outcome: Taken in October 930 and lost in 931; in late 938 the Han fleet under Liu Hongcao met Ngo Quyen's at the Bach Dang River and 'half of the Han army died, either killed or drowned, including Liu Hongcao'; Liu Yan turned back to Guangzhou and Ngo Quyen proclaimed himself king in spring 939.
wars.note: The Southern Han page counts only the two campaigns of 931 and 938 and says both failed.

notes: Cliopatria row Southern Han 911-979 (4 shapes). Corrections: (1) it includes northern Vietnam to 946 (bbox to 17.77 N, countries China and Vietnam), which no opened page supports: Jinghai was a Viet principality that Southern Han occupied only from October 930 to 931 and failed to take in 938 (Bach Dang page). The ngo-dynasty dossier (se-01) records its 939 founding as taken from southern-han and the 947 Cliopatria shape change as the loss of that land; that dossier should treat 939 as the end of Jinghai's autonomy under Duong Dinh Nghe / Kieu Cong Tien rather than a Southern Han loss, or mark the Jinghai circuit as its predecessor. (2) The state ends in 971 with the Song capture of Guangzhou, not 979. (3) From winter 951 the Guilin and Wuzhou countries come from the fallen Chu (Southern Tang page: 'to secure Lingnan'); the southern-chu dossier has no matching 951 loss to southern-han (it loses Hunan to the Southern Tang and ends) and should add one, with the 908 gain it already carries. The Southern Tang page names no prefecture, so those discs are a reading. Start year: the infobox says 'Established: 917' and Liu Yan proclaimed Yue in 917, but the Tang fell in 907 and Cliopatria draws the state from 911, so the dossier starts in 907 to cover the 908 loss; the 917 and 918 events are renames. Disagreement: the Southern Han page says Liu Yin died in 917; the Ma Yin page has Liu Yan as Liu Yin's successor asking for a Ma bride in 913, so the 905-917 regime is Liu Yin's then Liu Yan's with the page dates unreconciled. The rulers list starts at 917 for that reason. Not placed because the pages cannot: Liu Yin's 911 taking of Rong and Gao from Ma's man Yao Yanzhang (Ma Yin page names the prefectures, not the places; the Cliopatria shape already holds the south coast). The Southern Han page says Min and Chu fell to the Southern Tang in 945 and 951 and that the Southern Tang then 'occupied all of the northern boundary'; no Southern Han loss is dated. Counterpart needing a dossier: Jinghai circuit (the Khuc clan, Duong Dinh Nghe, Kieu Cong Tien, 905-939), suggested slug jinghai-circuit, for se-01. Infobox gives no area, so no ratio against Cliopatria's 322,737 km2. The budget was five pages; seven were opened (the Five Dynasties and Ma Chu pages are shared with other states, the Ma Chu page turned out silent).
